identity.title: Online Learning and Equilibrium Computation with Ranking Feedback

problem.claim: The paper studies online learning when the learner observes only rankings over proposed actions, including instantaneous-utility and time-average-utility rankings under full-information and bandit feedback.

gap.claim: Existing online learning algorithms generally depend on numeric utility feedback, which may be unavailable or privacy-restricted in human-in-the-loop settings.

contributions.claim: Shows that sublinear external regret is generally impossible with instantaneous-utility ranking feedback, and also impossible for time-average ranking feedback under sufficiently low-temperature Plackett–Luce rankings.
Develops algorithms achieving sublinear regret when the utility sequence has sublinear total variation; for full-information time-average rankings, the extra variation assumption can be removed.
Shows that using the algorithms by all players yields an approximate coarse correlated equilibrium, and demonstrates them in an online large-language-model routing task.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present an online learning model based solely on ranking feedback and develop algorithms with the stated regret guarantees under ranking-specific conditions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report impossibility of sublinear external regret for instantaneous-utility rankings in general.
The authors report sublinear-regret algorithms under sublinear total variation, with the variation requirement removable in the full-information time-average setting.
The authors report an approximate coarse correlated equilibrium consequence and an online LLM-routing demonstration.

narrative_sequence.summary: Numeric utility feedback can be unavailable or privacy-sensitive, motivating ranking-only feedback.
The study defines instantaneous and time-average ranking mechanisms under full-information and bandit feedback.
It reports impossibility results for instantaneous rankings and, under sufficiently deterministic Plackett–Luce rankings, time-average rankings.
It introduces sublinear-regret algorithms under sublinear utility variation, with a stronger full-information time-average result.
The abstract reports equilibrium and LLM-routing applications.

source_observation.claim: The abstract places impossibility results before algorithmic guarantees and states the additional assumptions under which guarantees hold.

lessons.interpretation: Separating information-theoretic limits from conditional positive results makes the scope of a method easier to assess.
lessons.application: Frame a learning paper by first identifying feedback regimes where the target guarantee is impossible, then state each sufficient assumption alongside its guarantee.
lessons.exception: This structure is less suitable when the work is primarily descriptive or has no meaningful impossibility or boundary result.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify regret rates, action-space assumptions, variation bounds, temperature threshold, algorithm details, or the quantitative routing results.
The equilibrium approximation and routing demonstration lack quantitative conditions and outcomes in the abstract.
